findings.F1: The test missed the bar only because its supporting check could not be computed, not because the effect was weak. The forecast sits at its cap of -20 on 84 % of the 1,048 event bars in folds B and C, so the median of |forecast| is -20 itself. The "strictly above the median" deeper half is therefore empty and the check returned None. Meanwhile the main measure confirms: +0.59 % per case, t 3.54, over 922 days.
findings.F2: Measured on the run's own percent loss rather than on the saturated forecast, the grading the idea predicts is clearly present. The deeper half of runs (per coin) is followed by a +1.99 % short-direction excess next day (t 4.15, 522 cases). The shallower half gets +0.08 % (t 0.32, 526 cases). The difference is +1.91 % with Welch t 5.77, and Spearman between depth and excess is 0.16 (p 1e-7).
findings.F3: The depth quintiles rise toward the deep end: +0.53 %, -0.09 %, +0.54 %, +1.55 % (t 2.88) and +2.64 % (t 3.46), about 210 cases each. Run length grades nothing: 2-day runs give +1.08 %, 3-day +0.80 %, 4-day +0.51 %, 5+ days +2.21 %.

ideas.name: depth-graded run-break fade, wider
ideas.idea: An up day that ends a run of down days is followed by a fall over the next day, and that fall is larger the more the price dropped over the run of down days it ends.
ideas.consequence: A trader fading run breaks should size the short by how far the run fell, not by how many days it lasted, because shallow runs give back almost nothing.

ideas.idea: An up day that ends a run of down days is followed by a fall over the next day, and that fall is larger the more the price dropped over the run of down days it ends, measured against the coin's usual daily swing over the last 30 days.
ideas.consequence: A trader fading run breaks should size the short by how many of the coin's usual daily swings the run fell, since runs that are shallow for the coin give back nothing and deep ones give back about 2 % the next day.
ideas.name: swing-scaled run-break fade
